reading: Every isolated marker (colour 1) draws a full-width row line and full-height column line of colour 1; the marker itself becomes 2 and its four diagonal neighbours become 3 (drawn on top of the lines).

new_rows.name: arms
new_rows.datalog: arms(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 1.

why: Stamp the constant 3x3 unit 313/121/313 centred on each marker, then each colour-1 arm cell extends outward to the grid border (inward/sideways rays stop at once on the stamp's own 2 and 3 cells). No line ever hits another marker's stamp in training or test.

reading: Colour-4 cells mark partial plus shapes (centre + 4 arms) inside a 0/5 noise field; the 5 cells that complete each plus become 2.

new_rows.name: plus5
new_rows.datalog:
inplus(CY, CX, Y, X) :- px(CY, CX, K), Y = CY, X = CX.
inplus(CY, CX, Y, X) :- px(CY, CX, K), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y = CY, X = CX + DX, px(Y, X, K2).
inplus(CY, CX, Y, X) :- px(CY, CX, K), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y = CY + DY, X = CX, px(Y, X, K2).
ok45(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 4.
ok45(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), C = 5.
bad(CY, CX) :- inplus(CY, CX, Y, X), !ok45(Y, X).
c4(CY, CX, Y, X) :- inplus(CY, CX, Y, X), px(Y, X, C), C = 4, !bad(CY, CX).
cand(CY, CX) :- c4(CY, CX, Y, X).
n4(CY, CX, count(Y, X)) :- c4(CY, CX, Y, X).
miss(CY, CX, EY, EX) :- c4(CY, CX, Y, X), cand(EY, EX), !c4(EY, EX, Y, X).
dom(CY, CX) :- cand(CY, CX), cand(EY, EX), !miss(CY, CX, EY, EX), n4(CY, CX, N), n4(EY, EX, M), M > N.
valid(CY, CX) :- n4(CY, CX, N), N > 1, !dom(CY, CX).
plus5(Y, X) :- valid(CY, CX), inplus(CY, CX, Y, X), px(Y, X, C), C = 5.

why: A plus centre is valid when all its in-grid cells are 4 or 5, it holds at least two 4s, and no other candidate plus holds a strict superset of its 4s; exactly the 5s of valid pluses change, 5 -> 2.

reading: Every object that is a square outline (square box, whole box border filled; a 2x2 block counts) gets colour-2 marks on the two background cells orthogonally outside each of its four corners.

new_rows.name: sqmarks
new_rows.datalog:
fo(O, Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), cell(Y, X, C).
y0(O, min(Y)) :- fo(O, Y, X).
y1(O, max(Y)) :- fo(O, Y, X).
x0(O, min(X)) :- fo(O, Y, X).
x1(O, max(X)) :- fo(O, Y, X).
box(O, A, B, C, D) :- y0(O, A), y1(O, B), x0(O, C), x1(O, D).
sq(O) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), H = B - A, W = D - C, H = W.
edge(O, Y, X) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = A, X >= C, X <= D.
edge(O, Y, X) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = B, X >= C, X <= D.
edge(O, Y, X) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), X = C, Y >= A, Y <= B.
edge(O, Y, X) :- box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), X = D, Y >= A, Y <= B.
gap(O) :- edge(O, Y, X), !fo(O, Y, X).
ring(O) :- sq(O), !gap(O).
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = A - 1, X = C.
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = A, X = C - 1.
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = A - 1, X = D.
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = A, X = D + 1.
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = B + 1, X = C.
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = B, X = C - 1.
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = B + 1, X = D.
sqmarks(Y, X) :- ring(O), box(O, A, B, C, D), px(Y, X, K), Y = B, X = D + 1.

why: Only background cells next to the corners of square-outline objects change (7 -> 2); diagonal pairs, lines and non-square rectangles are left alone.

reading: The grey (5) shape is cut into 2x2 squares, painted 8, and straight 1x3 bars, painted 2.

slots.subject: the single colour-5 shape
slots.pieces: an exact tiling of the shape by 2x2 squares and 1x3 straight bars (horizontal or vertical)

why: Every 5 cell ends in exactly one 2x2 block of 8 or one 3-long straight run of 2; nothing else changes.

reading: A 6x6 block shows a 3x3 template drawn at 2x scale in colour c; in every 3x3 panel (between the 4-lines) whose 1-cells cover the template, the template cells turn from 1 to c.

slots.panels: 3x3 cells cut by the colour-4 separator lines
slots.template: the colour-c shape (c not in {0,1,4}) in its 4-framed block, downscaled by 2 to a 3x3 mask
slots.condition: every template position in the panel is 1

why: Changed cells are exactly the template positions inside panels that contain the template among their 1s, 1 -> c; all other cells stay.

reading: Each closed one-cell-wide outline has its corner cells recoloured: convex corners (the cell between the two arms is enclosed) become 4, concave corners become 2.

new_rows.name: convex
new_rows.datalog:
fg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bgp(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fg(Y, X).
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), Y = 0.
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), X = 0.
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), my(M), Y = M.
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), mx(M), X = M.
ext(Y2, X2) :- ext(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgp(Y2, X2).
inner(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), !ext(Y, X).
vert(A) :- off(A, Z), Z = 0.
horz(B) :- off(Z, B), Z = 0.
turn(Y, X, A, B) :- fg(Y, X), vert(A), horz(B), Y1 = Y + A, fg(Y1, X), X1 = X + B, fg(Y, X1), Y2 = Y - A, !fg(Y2, X), X2 = X - B, !fg(Y, X2).
convex(Y, X) :- turn(Y, X, A, B), Y1 = Y + A, X1 = X + B, inner(Y1, X1).

new_rows.name: concave
new_rows.datalog:
fg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bgp(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !fg(Y, X).
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
mx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), Y = 0.
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), X = 0.
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), my(M), Y = M.
ext(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), mx(M), X = M.
ext(Y2, X2) :- ext(Y, X), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, bgp(Y2, X2).
inner(Y, X) :- bgp(Y, X), !ext(Y, X).
vert(A) :- off(A, Z), Z = 0.
horz(B) :- off(Z, B), Z = 0.
turn(Y, X, A, B) :- fg(Y, X), vert(A), horz(B), Y1 = Y + A, fg(Y1, X), X1 = X + B, fg(Y, X1), Y2 = Y - A, !fg(Y2, X), X2 = X - B, !fg(Y, X2).
cvx(Y, X) :- turn(Y, X, A, B), Y1 = Y + A, X1 = X + B, inner(Y1, X1).
concave(Y, X) :- turn(Y, X, A, B), !cvx(Y, X).

why: A turn cell has exactly one vertical and one horizontal outline neighbour; if the diagonal cell between them is enclosed background it becomes 4, otherwise 2. Straight outline cells keep their colour (8, 3 or 1 in training).

reading: The 3x3 input has one all-one-colour row or column; the 9x9 output repeats the input three times along that row or column's band, and the rest is 0.
why: Output blocks on the band matching the uniform line's index are copies of the input; all other blocks are empty.

reading: The top and bottom rows are full lines of two colours; each object between them slides vertically toward the line of its own colour until it touches that line (or a piece already landed).

new_rows.name: pieces
new_rows.datalog:
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
pieces(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y > 0, my(M), Y < M.

why: Each single-colour object keeps its shape and column and ends in contact with the full border row of its colour. Caveat: pair 0's 3-tall colour-8 bar in the last column shows as 5 tall in the output, which no rigid move reproduces.

reading: In every column whose bottom cell is 5, each coloured cell paints its colour upward over the background until it reaches the next coloured cell above it (or the top border).

new_rows.name: gcol
new_rows.datalog:
my(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
gcol5(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), my(M), Y = M, C = 5.
gcol(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), gcol5(X).

why: Lines run upward only, from each source cell to just below the first non-background cell above it; columns without a 5 at the bottom do not change.

reading: The 3x9 grid is three 3x3 blocks, each holding a grey pattern; each block is painted entirely in a colour set by its pattern (top row -> 6, ring -> 3, bottom row -> 1, anti-diagonal -> 9, centre dot -> 4).

slots.blocks: the three 3x3 blocks side by side (no separator lines)
slots.action: fill the whole block with key(pattern)

why: Each output block is uniform, and its colour depends only on that block's input pattern, the same way in every pair.
